API Integration

Building API Integrations That Recover From Failures

Design timeouts, retries, idempotency and useful error messages so an interrupted request does not become a lost or duplicated transaction.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read

In this guide

A timeout does not prove failureClassify the problemMake retries deliberateDesign a support queueTest ambiguous outcomes

A timeout does not prove failure

Your server may stop waiting even though the provider completed the operation. That distinction matters when creating an order or charging a payment. Before retrying, understand whether the original action might already exist. A robust integration tracks the intended operation rather than treating every network request as a new business event.

Classify the problem

Invalid input usually needs correction. Missing permission requires configuration or access changes. A temporary unavailable service may justify a delayed retry. Return enough information for the appropriate person to act, but avoid exposing credentials or internal stack traces. A single “Something went wrong” message hides these different recovery paths.

Make retries deliberate

Use bounded attempts and increasing delays for transient failures, respecting provider instructions. For operations that change state, use the provider’s idempotency mechanism when available. MDN distinguishes method semantics, but the actual business operation still needs careful design: never assume that retrying an arbitrary POST request is harmless.

Design a support queue

Record a correlation identifier, operation type, safe error code and status. Let authorized staff inspect pending or failed operations and retry through a controlled path. Avoid using customer text or entire payloads as a default log entry. Support needs enough context to diagnose the issue, not an unnecessary copy of sensitive data.

Test ambiguous outcomes

Simulate a slow response after the provider accepts a request. Verify that retrying produces one record and that the customer can discover the final result. Also test validation errors and provider outages. The goal is a predictable recovery story, including what the user should do next and who owns unresolved cases.
